title: Down the TOBA route: Shreveport and Mobile
summary: The show moves through Galveston, Shreveport and Mobile, where he meets Lannie Scott, George Lewis and Professor Campbell.

story.theme_name: Medicine shows, minstrels, circuses and the black theater circuit
story.community_name: On the road with minstrel, carnival and tent shows

blocks.x: So how long did you stay with the show?
We left Galveston in...left Bull Herschel with a broken heart, and then we went to Shreveport. And
*Mayo Williams was the recording director for seven selections Smith recorded, January 14-15, 1929; Smith recorded "Pine Top's Boogie-Woogie" on December 29, 1928.

Shreveport is where I first met Lannie Scott and met George Lewis and...let's see...Professor Campbell had the band, in the Star Theater in Shreveport. And from Shreveport we went to Mobile, Alabama. And all the time, Danny, each week we were meeting different people. Different shows of 20 people, or 30 people or 10 people, you know, like that. When we got to Louisville, that's when I first met Art Tatum. And then you had Cow Cow Davenport, you had many of those guys, you know, of that day. But Art and I became close friends later...much later we became you know really pals, you know. Because I didn't see him from that time until I saw him in Chicago with Adelaide Hall in the early 30s. And this is...I think Joe Turner was with Adelaide at that time. She had three piano players, didn't she? Or did she have two...
